newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Zeitler-no need for change in rate trend.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Zeitler-no need for change in rate trend.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler on Tuesday said that he saw no need for a change in the trend of German interest rates at this time.
"Based on the fundamental factors I see no reason for a change of direction in interest rates," said Zeitler, who is also the president of the state central bank in Bavaria.
Zeitler cited Germany's low inflation rate, currently running at 1.4 percent in West Germany, and the government's efforts to pare back budget deficits.
The Bank of England this morning stunned financial markets when it raised interest rates to 6.25 percent from 6.0 percent to prevent inflation from getting out of hand.
In late March the U.S. Fed ended its two year easing period when it raised interest rates to guard against revived inflationary pressures.
Independent economists have said that the Bundesbank might need to raise its interest rates as soon as this fall to avoid a possible overheating.
The Bundesbank last raised interest rates in the summer of 1992. It last cut its key discount and Lombard rates to 2.50 and 4.50 respectively in April 1996.
The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was cut to three percent last August.
